Entretanto, las fuerzas gubernamentales de Yemen se retiraron de una zona cercana al estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb para, sostienen, centrarse en la defensa de su base principal en Adén. item.title: US probes nationwide flights stoppage as travel disruptions persist
item.description: US air travel is expected to return to normal this Sunday, following a nationwide ground stop Friday night that stranded hundreds of thousands of passengers and disrupted travel worldwide. The Trump administration blamed the incident on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines and said there was no evidence this was a cyberattack. The ground stop now raises questions about the country's aging infrastructure and lawmakers are calling for an investigation. Analysis by Philip Mann, aviation expert at Vector Strategic Consulting. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Chinese spy, chip sales, Trump ties... The Nvidia scandal deepens
item.description: The Nvidia scandal continues to unravel. Sunday, the Singapore-based company Megaspeed said that Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang had officially left the company in 2025. She is the alleged Chinese spy that had an affair with Nvidia's former CEO Jensen Huang. Late last year, revelations showed she was being investigated for chip smuggling. The scandal has also raised questions about how much the US government knew – Trump was allegedly warned about the affair but did not react. Analysis by Laïla Mörch, CEO of Shael and tech investor in Paris. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: Elon Musk's SpaceX aborts booster recovery due to technical issues
item.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX is in the midst of a 15th test-flight of its Starship rocket. The company was hoping to pull off the first-ever "double catch" - with both the booster and the ship itself coming safely back down to earth. Instead, an unspecified problem forced the company to abort recovery of the booster, which was diverted from its return path and crashed down into the Gulf of Mexico. Analysis by journalist Frédéric Castel, based in Bosa Chica, Texas, USA. Fuente: France 24 - English.

item.title: World's largest freshwater lake is recovering after decades of decline
item.description: Lake Baikal in Siberia holds around 20% of the world's surface freshwater, making it the most voluminous freshwater lake (Lake Superior on the United States–Canada border is the largest by surface area). This makes the lake one of the most important environments for biodiversity—in fact, it was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1996 because of this. Yet it has shown considerable decline over the last century, with aridification spreading across East Asia. Fuente: Phys.org.
